rv.q: Invisible Me is a delightful, uplifting play that makes me look forward to reaching the age of 60.

INVISIBLE ME charts the somewhat interconnectedness of three individuals, all of whom are on the cusp of turning 60 and are determined one way or another to demonstrate that there's life in the (nearly) old dog yet, at least before the inevitable and imminent descent into decrepitude.
The result is a piece that earns its uplift without softening its emotional edge.

cn.t: Critics praise this warm, uplifting play about loneliness and dating after 60, with reviewers calling it "delightful" and "moving" in its portrayal of three newly single sexagenarians navigating invisibility and connection in later life.
